name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=text_dialog, descriptor=typewriter_loop. No address residue. Name accurately reflects the function: it runs the Yes/No prompt's typewriter glyph animation plus the keyboard input loop. Verified against decompilation and against caller fd2_run_revive_menu_main which uses the return as a Yes/No confirm.
purpose: Yes/No confirmation prompt: drives the per-glyph typewriter dialog animation and the keyboard input loop, returning whether the user confirmed (Enter/Space) or cancelled (Esc).
logic_summary: Snapshots mode-13h VRAM (0xA0000) into the slide-composed work buffer and copies the full 200x320 page into the game-state work buffer; when battle_tile_map>1 it primes the battle base scene. Plays a 4-frame intro that folds the two Yes/No corner sprites outward (left -4/frame, right +4/frame). Main loop is throttled on the BIOS tick word @0x46C (advances only when delta >= 2 ticks or wrapped): each accepted frame ticks blink_phase_oscillator (0x53C13) 0..3, optionally re-composites the battle scene, runs the typewriter state machine (char_phase==1 paints the current glyph via blit_normal when battle_tile_map==0 else blit_mirrored and reseeds the inter-glyph pace = rng%0x1E+10; otherwise counts the pace down and on 0 starts the next glyph at offset *(portrait_buf+0xC) and re-arms char_phase), copies the work buffer back to the framebuffer (full page when battle_tile_map<2 else the small in-battle band), and draws the two Yes/No boxes (selector = corner_state[i]*3 + oscillator/2 on the selected box) flushed via blit_rectangle. On a keypress it reads INT 16h via int386 and dispatches the scancode: Enter/Space/extended/Numpad-0 -> return 1; Esc/Numpad-. -> return -1; Left -> cursor=0(Yes); Right -> cursor=1(No); else keep looping. The blink oscillator is reset to 0 on every exit path. Initial pace seed is rng%0x1E+2, the per-glyph reseed is rng%0x1E+10 (both seeded from a fresh fd2_advance_rng_state(); Ghidra's clobbered-register rendering is the known EAX-tracking bug). Body ends with a tail-call JMP 0x13FCC into a shared Watcom cleanup epilogue.

returns.semantics: 1 = advance / Yes confirmed (Enter/Space/extended/Numpad-0 pressed); -1 = cancel (Esc/Numpad-.). The actual Yes vs No selection is carried separately in data_fd2_ui_menu_cursor_idx (0=Yes,1=No); callers treat (ret != -1 && cursor==0) as a Yes.
